#: Scrub manifest for the servarr collector: the documents its acquisition path fetches from every configured instance — /system/status, /health, /queue/status, /queue and /history — plus the two halves of the capture that are not documents at all. `instances` is the fleet receipt (which instances were configured, on which API family, and which receipts were absent), and `response-codes` records the requests that answered with a STATUS and no body, which is what prowlarr's missing /queue is.
#credential: The API key appears in NO payload and cannot: it rides the X-Api-Key request header, never a URL and never a response body, and the capture never asks the receipt for it — a `secret` classification refuses the whole run, and rightly, because DESIGN 21 says a secret must never have been captured at all. The instance URL is not captured either: it is pure location (`http://<host>:7878`) and nothing in a replay dials it, so the honest treatment is not to ask for it. Both are supplied by the replay seam as a replay-invalid stand-in (see fleet_specs in harness/bin/se-reference-collector).
#names:
A BOUND, stated where the reader is, because nothing mechanical can enforce it. An instance name is OPERATOR-CHOSEN — it is whatever SE_SERVARR_INSTANCES says — and in this capture the two are `radarr` and `prowlarr`, the products' own names, identical on every estate that runs them and naming nothing here. So they are classified `nothing`, on the same reading harness/scrub/docker.json applies to container and image names.

What makes this bound sharper than docker's is that the name is unavoidably published: it is in every payload FILE NAME (radarr-api-v3-health.json), which no manifest entry reaches and no scrubber touches; it is the `App` fact on every row; and it is the first half of every object id (`health:radarr/IndexerRssCheck`). A capture whose operator named an instance after a host, a person or a purpose — after the machine it runs on, after whoever it serves, after the library it manages — publishes that word in a dozen places this file cannot govern, and re-classifying `*.name` would not remove one of them. Such a capture must be renamed at the source or not taken.
#messages:
Health messages and the instance's own display name take `content` with format `prose`, which is the ruling of 2026-08-19: unbounded text may honestly carry no identifier, so finding nothing is not a refusal, and it still takes the same free-text pass every formatless entry takes — so a hostname or an address written inside one is still substituted. That is strictly stronger than classifying them `nothing`, and it costs nothing on this capture, where every message is the app's own generic diagnosis (`No indexers enabled, Prowlarr will not return search results`) and instanceName is the product's default.

The residue: the free-text pass substitutes names, addresses and identifiers, NOT filesystem paths. A health message on a host with real libraries names them — `Missing root folder: /media/films` is one of the commonest items these apps raise — and a path is location. A capture from such a host needs `*.message` re-argued before it is scrubbed; prose is what keeps the ordinary case honest, not a claim that the field is safe.
#paths: startupPath, appData and urlBase are filesystem-shaped and are classified `nothing` for THIS capture, which is a bound and not a property of the field. Both apps run from the linuxserver.io container images, so `/app/radarr/bin` and `/config` are the image's own layout — identical for everyone who pulls the same tag, exactly like the mount points harness/scrub/docker.json publishes — and urlBase is the empty string because neither app sits behind a path prefix. A bare-metal install puts an operator-chosen directory in the first two and a reverse-proxy prefix in the third, and all three become location. Nothing mechanical will force that re-reading.
#unreached:
Not classified here because no path in this capture reaches them, and a manifest entry for a shape nobody captured is a claim nobody checked (the rule harness/scrub/traefik.json states). Four families:

  · `records.*` — the queue and history documents are both empty on this guest, so every member of a queue record (title, indexer, downloadClient, downloadId, errorMessage, statusMessages) and of a history event (sourceTitle, data.*, quality) is unclassified. Those are the members that carry release titles (content), indexer names (content), and — in a grab's `data.downloadUrl` — an indexer's api key or a private tracker's passkey, which is `secret` and would refuse the run outright. That refusal is the correct answer: a capture from an app with a live queue must extend this file first, and the adapter's own evidence route already withholds those URL tails (_redact_history_urls).
  · `instances.*.missing` and `instances.*.duplicates` — both empty, because both instances carry complete receipts. They hold environment VARIABLE NAMES (`SE_RADARR_URL`), never values.
  · The `/downloadclient` document, which get_object fetches for the dispatches-to edges and the acquisition path never does. Its entries carry download-client hostnames and, in their fields, credentials.
  · A non-404 response code. `response-codes` is classified below, and 404 is the only status the replay seam will replay — see REPLAYABLE_CODES.
#~key: The root keys of every document whose root is an object. Two kinds sit here and both are `nothing`. In /system/status, /queue, /queue/status and /history they are the apps' own schema words — appName, totalRecords, sortDirection — identical on every install. In `response-codes` they are payload stems (`prowlarr-api-v1-queue`), which carry the instance name and the request path: the path is the API's own vocabulary and the name is bounded by #names above. The entry exists at all because the pattern language asks for it — an unscoped `*.…` entry walks some dict's keys with a `*` at every document's root, and _keys_are_data reads that as a claim that the keys are data.
